_comment: THE NEWSLETTER'S MCP SURFACE — DECLARED, NEVER INHERITED, AND EMPTY.
Used with `claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config deploy/newsletter_mcp.json`,
which makes this file the ONLY source of MCP servers for that process.
ZERO SERVERS IS THE POINT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The weekly letter is a
narrative process: it reads research_store/newsletters/facts.json (written
by scripts/letter_facts.py before it starts), fills newsletter/template.html
and writes one HTML file. Every number it is allowed to state is already on
disk — prompts/newsletter.md forbids it computing one — so it needs no
broker, no market feed and no agentic-trader server. Its intended authority
over live money is ZERO, and an empty file is how that is spelled.
WHAT THIS REMOVES. Until now the letter was spawned as `claude -p --model
... --settings deploy/loop_settings.json <prompt>` with no MCP flags at
all, so it inherited every server the box offers. Enumerated on this droplet
2026-08-23 with `claude mcp list` from the repo root: 21 servers, including
robinhood-trading (THE live execution venue), agentic-trader, and three
other brokers with live trading surfaces — Interactive Brokers, webull and
Public.com — plus 15 unrelated claude.ai account connectors. The shared
settings file then ALLOWED mcp__robinhood-trading__place_equity_order and
cancel_equity_order, so the process that writes prose could place and cancel
real orders in the Agentic account. That was never anyone's intent; it was
inherited.
⛔ DO NOT ADD A SERVER HERE. If the letter ever appears to need live data,
the fix is a deterministic script that writes the figure into facts.json
before the model runs — that is the existing architecture (the letter
narrates, letter_facts.py calculates), and it keeps the narrator's
authority at zero. A read-only broker server is still a broker server: the
trading sessions' allowlist was 'never the hole' either, right up until a
capability added for one role widened another.
⛔ NO SECRETS HERE, AND NONE MAY BE ADDED — this file is committed.
